column9: Seen from the foot of the bed, Joseph (governor), displeased, takes hold of his father's right hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's, but Jacob (old) refuses, keeping it on Ephraim and saying that the younger shall be greater than the firstborn; Manasseh and Ephraim kneel side by side before the bed.

column8: Exactly four people; Joseph is in his fifties, his sons grown young men. No sword or bow shown.
column9: In the same room, Jacob (old), lying back on his bed, holds his son's hand and tells him that he is dying, but that God will be with them and bring them again to the land of their fathers; Joseph (governor) kneels close beside the bed, and Manasseh and Ephraim stand quietly behind their father.

column8: Exactly thirteen people: Jacob and his twelve sons, Joseph among them, all men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded. No women, children or servants.
column9: In a plain room open to the pastures of Goshen, Jacob (old) sits up on his bed as his twelve sons gather around him in a wide half-circle, Joseph (governor) among them in his Egyptian linen; Reuben, the firstborn, stands before his father with his head bowed as Jacob speaks of his strength and his failing, and Joseph's brothers watch solemnly.

column8: Exactly thirteen people: Jacob and his twelve sons, men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded. The same room and light as before. No weapons.
column9: In the same room, Jacob (old) turns his face aside and raises a hand in rebuke toward two of Joseph's brothers, Simeon and Levi, who stand before the bed with lowered heads as he curses their fierce anger and cruel wrath; the other sons, Joseph (governor) among them, look on uneasily.

column8: Only one person: Judah. One young lion and one donkey's foal. No brothers bowing and no crowd.
column9: Pictured from Jacob's words over Judah: Judah sits on a rocky height holding a sceptre, a young lion couched on the rock beside him, and below him a donkey's foal is tied to a choice vine heavy with ripe grapes, the hillside around it rich with vines and the grapes dark as wine.

column8: No people anywhere. One strong donkey lying down with two loads.
column9: Pictured from Jacob's words: on one side a sheltered haven of the sea where ships ride at anchor along the shore, and on the other a pleasant green land at rest, where a strong donkey lies couched between two heavy burdens slung on either side of it, its shoulder bowed to bear them.

column4: Dan, a serpent by the way
column8: Exactly one horse, one rider and one adder; nothing else on the path. No town and no judge.
column9: Pictured from Jacob's words over Dan: on a narrow, stony path through the hills, an adder lying in the path strikes at the heels of a horse, which rears up, and its rider, a man in a plain robe, tips backward from its back, about to fall; the path is otherwise empty.

column8: Exactly thirteen people: Jacob and his twelve sons, men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded; three of them stand before the bed. No raiders, battle or deer.
column9: In the same room, Jacob (old) speaks from his bed to three of Joseph's brothers, Gad, Asher and Naphtali, who stand before him with bowed heads to receive their blessings: Gad's of overcoming at the last, Asher's of rich bread, Naphtali's of a hind let loose; the other sons, Joseph (governor) among them, look on.

column8: No people anywhere. No archers and no weapons.
column9: Pictured from Jacob's words over Joseph: a fruitful bough, heavy with fruit, grows beside an old stone well, its branches running up and over a high wall; beyond the wall the everlasting hills roll away into the distance under a wide, bright sky, and the whole land lies rich and peaceful.

column8: Exactly thirteen people: Jacob and his twelve sons, men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded; Benjamin, the youngest, is a grown man. No women, children or servants. No rain.
column9: In the same room, Jacob (old) turns to Benjamin, the youngest of Joseph's brothers, a grown man, who kneels before the bed as the last to be blessed, and speaks over him of a ravening wolf; the eleven other sons, Joseph (governor) among them, stand around the bed in a wide circle, each one blessed with his own blessing.

column8: Exactly thirteen people: Jacob and his twelve sons, men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded. No women, children or servants.
column9: Jacob (old), having charged his sons to bury him with his fathers in the cave of Machpelah, gathers up his feet into the bed and lies back, his eyes closing in peace as he breathes his last; his twelve sons, Joseph (governor) and Joseph's brothers, stand around the bed with bowed heads.

column8: Exactly thirteen people: Jacob lying dead, Joseph and his eleven brothers, men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded. No physicians and no mourners yet.
column9: In the room where Jacob died, Joseph (governor) has fallen upon his father's face, weeping over him and kissing him, as Jacob (old) lies still on his bed with his eyes closed; Joseph's brothers stand around the bed with bowed heads, weeping, in the quiet daylight.

column8: Pharaoh is not in this picture: Joseph speaks to the officials of Pharaoh's house. Joseph is in his fifties.
column9: In a columned court of Pharaoh's palace, Joseph (governor) stands before Egyptians of Pharaoh's house, officials in white linen, asking them to speak in Pharaoh's ears for him: his father made him swear to bury him in his grave in Canaan, and he asks leave to go up and bury him and come again; the officials listen with sympathy.

column8: No coffin. No little ones, flocks or herds: they were left in Goshen. Jacob's sons, men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded, carry his body.
column9: Seen from a high ridge, a very great company winds out of Egypt across the desert: chariots and horsemen go before and behind, Pharaoh's servants and the elders of Egypt, Egyptians in white linen, walk in the middle, and Joseph (governor) and Joseph's brothers carry their father's embalmed body, wrapped in linen on a bier, as dust rises into the sky.

column4: Mourning at the floor of Atad
column8: No coffin. No little ones, flocks or herds. Jacob's sons are men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded.
column9: At the threshing floor of Atad beyond the Jordan, under a heavy grey sky, the great company sits around Jacob's body, wrapped in linen on its bier, mourning with a great and very sore lamentation, Joseph (governor) and Joseph's brothers nearest to it and the Egyptians around them, while Canaanites of the land watch in wonder from a nearby hillside.

column4: Buried in the cave of Machpelah
column8: Exactly twelve brothers carrying their father, men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded; the rest of the company is not shown. No coffin.
column9: In the field before Mamre, Jacob's twelve sons, Joseph (governor) among them with Joseph's brothers, carry their father's body, wrapped in linen on a bier, across the open field toward the dark mouth of the cave of Machpelah in a rocky hillside at its end, to bury him there as he commanded them.

column8: Exactly eleven brothers on their faces before Joseph, men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded; Joseph is in his fifties. No messenger and no children.
column9: At ground level in the courtyard of Joseph's house in soft morning light, Joseph's brothers fall down on their faces on the paved floor before him, begging forgiveness for the evil they did him and saying that they are his servants; Joseph (governor) stands before them, weeping at their fear.

column8: Exactly eleven brothers, men of middle age or older, some grey-bearded; Joseph is in his fifties. No children and no onlookers.
column9: Seen from a little above in the courtyard, Joseph (governor) bends to raise his brothers from the ground, reaching out his hands to them and telling them not to fear, for God meant it unto good, and he will nourish them and their little ones; Joseph's brothers rise with relief and tears on their faces.

column8: Joseph is a very old man. With him only small children of his family; no crowd.
column9: In a garden of his house in Egypt, in the warm afternoon, Joseph (old), white-haired and very aged, sits in a carved chair beneath a spreading sycamore fig with a small child of Machir's family on his knees, while other little children of his sons' families sit and play at his feet.

column8: No coffin, bones or mummy. Joseph is very old, near death.
column9: In a quiet room of his house, Joseph (old), very aged, lies on his bed and lifts his hand as his brethren, white-bearded old men, and younger men of the children of Israel gather around him and swear to carry his bones up out of Egypt to the land God swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.
